answer_text:
We count binary strings of length \(10\) that avoid both substrings \(101\) and \(010\).

Since these forbidden substrings have length \(3\), it is enough to track the last two bits of a valid string. The possible states are

\[
00,\quad 01,\quad 10,\quad 11.
\]

Let

\[
A_n=\#\text{ valid strings of length }n\text{ ending in }00,
\]
\[
B_n=\#\text{ valid strings of length }n\text{ ending in }01,
\]
\[
C_n=\#\text{ valid strings of length }n\text{ ending in }10,
\]
\[
D_n=\#\text{ valid strings of length }n\text{ ending in }11.
\]

Now determine the allowed transitions:

- From \(00\), we may append \(0\) or \(1\), giving \(00\) or \(01\).
- From \(01\), we may append only \(1\), because appending \(0\) gives \(010\).
- From \(10\), we may append only \(0\), because appending \(1\) gives \(101\).
- From \(11\), we may append \(0\) or \(1\), giving \(10\) or \(11\).

Thus for \(n\ge 2\),

\[
A_{n+1}=A_n+C_n,
\]
\[
B_{n+1}=A_n,
\]
\[
C_{n+1}=D_n,
\]
\[
D_{n+1}=B_n+D_n.
\]

By symmetry, swapping \(0\) and \(1\), we have

\[
A_n=D_n,\qquad B_n=C_n.
\]

Let

\[
x_n=A_n=D_n,\qquad y_n=B_n=C_n.
\]

Then the recurrences become

\[
x_{n+1}=x_n+y_n,
\]
\[
y_{n+1}=x_n.
\]

For length \(2\), all four strings are valid, so

\[
x_2=1,\qquad y_2=1.
\]

Now compute up to length \(10\):

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
n & x_n & y_n & \text{total}=2x_n+2y_n\\
\hline
2 & 1 & 1 & 4\\
3 & 2 & 1 & 6\\
4 & 3 & 2 & 10\\
5 & 5 & 3 & 16\\
6 & 8 & 5 & 26\\
7 & 13 & 8 & 42\\
8 & 21 & 13 & 68\\
9 & 34 & 21 & 110\\
10 & 55 & 34 & 178
\end{array}
\]

Therefore, the number of binary strings of length \(10\) that do not contain \(101\) or \(010\) is

\[
\boxed{178}.
\]
